Triage (2026-09-20T16:59Z): lands in `domain:cli` · `priority:p3` · type `Task`.

**Lane `domain:cli`.** `ObjectStackClient` is `packages/client*`, which the 域车道 table assigns to this lane.

**Grade `p3`, and the filing dev's own reading is why.** It recorded this and **declined to file**, on the grounds that it fits none of the three filing classes — and that is right: the 14 methods are **deliberate** (#12036 states the reason), so there is ⛔ no reproducible defect, ⛔ no violated declared contract, and ⛔ no metadata trap. Nothing is wrong on the tree today.

What is open is a **ratchet hole**: `check:exported-any-returns` asks **IS-any**, never **CONTAINS-any**, and the sites carry no annotation for a textual check to see. ⇒ the family is held by a prose docblock alone, and a **15th** method lands green.

⇒ 北极星「优先级」2's third arm — 不在路上、不在清单上 ⇒ `p3` — and `p3` rather than 不做, because the 仪器 test is answerable with a named consequence: 「一次放过假货的复核」, the 15th member entering with nothing to object.

Type `Task`: there is no defect to fix; the work is deciding whether the ratchet should see this class at all, and building it if so.

## ⚠️ For the claimant — the first question is NOT 「how do we detect CONTAINS-any」

It is **whether the family should be guarded mechanically at all**. #12036 made the 14 deliberate for a stated reason; if that reason still holds, the honest outcome may be an explicit annotation at the sites (so text CAN see them) rather than a widened ratchet that would have to carry 14 permanent exemptions on day one. ⛔ A gate born with a 14-entry exemption list is the shape this repo keeps filing cards about.

⚠️ Re-read `#11927`'s ratchet scope line before writing: a scope line that claims a coverage the matcher does not have is the second half of this card, and it is the half that misleads.

Size/model suggestion: S for the decision; ⛔ do not size the implementation before it.

## ⛔ Read this first: what this card is NOT

⛔ **`check:exported-any-returns` is not wrong.** Its IS-`any` scope is what buys it **zero false positives**, which is what makes it enforceable at all, and its ledger `$comment` states that scope line and the reason for it. #11927 built it to stop the 52nd IS-`any` site, and it does.

⛔ **Do not widen IS-any to CONTAINS-any across the package.** Caller-shaped `any` is a class the ledger deliberately protects — better-auth organisation metadata, an opaque OAuth client row. Widening would refuse them.

⇒ this card is about **a family the ratchet's documented scope leaves outside it**, ⛔ not about the ratchet.

## The shape

**14** methods in `ObjectStackClient.environments.*` (and nested `environments.packages.*`) return types that **contain** `any` and carry **no return annotation**. They are deliberate — #12036, whose reason hardened when ruling B on #16325 moved the cloud contracts out of this repo entirely (`packages/spec/src/cloud` measured **absent** on `origin/main`).

⚠️ Nothing mechanical holds the family:

| would-be guard | why it cannot see them |
|---|---|
| `check:exported-any-returns` | asks whether a return type **IS** `any`, ⛔ never whether it **CONTAINS** one |
| any text search | the sites carry **no return annotation at all** — `any` / `Promise` / `unwrapResponse` need never appear on the signature line |

⇒ ⭐ **a prose docblock is the only thing holding this family. A 15th such method would land silently green.**

## ⭐ The first act is a CENSUS, and ⛔ NOT with a grep

⚠️ This is the same lineage (#8140 → #11925 → #12104) whose whole thesis is that the population is **invisible to text search**. The #11925 round built the right instrument and its readings are on that card: a `ts.createProgram` + `TypeChecker` census asking **two halves separately** — (a) does the declaration node write an explicit return type (**source AST**, invisible in a built `.d.ts` because `tsup` always emits one), and (b) does `checker.getAwaitedType` **contain** `any` (**type**, invisible to text).

⇒ **re-derive the count and the membership with a checker-based census**, ⛔ never a text search. Report the instrument and why it sees what a grep cannot.

⚠️ ⭐ **Include a control, and audit the bucket you expect to be boring.** #11925's instrument had a **false negative** on its first version — `Record<string, any>[]` landed in the *clean* bucket because `Record<…>` resolves to a **mapped** type whose `typeArguments` is empty. It was found by reading the clean bucket, ⛔ not by assuming it, and the fix moved the reading 17 → 18.

## Then the decision this card exists for

**Does this family want a guard of its own?** The card's own suggestion is an allow-list pinned to the known sites, so that a 15th is **a diff someone must justify** rather than a silent addition.

⛔ **Do not build and land a guard in this round** unless your census shows the design is trivially settled — and say which it is. ⭐ *"No guard is worth it, and here is the measured reason"* is a **complete outcome**, the same shape as #19371's verdict and #19246's non-reproduction.

⚠️ If you do propose a guard, answer: **what does it refuse, what does it cost per new method, and what is its false-positive rate against the caller-shaped `any` the ledger protects?**

## Fences

⛔ Never edit `content/docs/releases/`. ⛔ `packages/spec/**` is the spec seat's. Changeset: ⛔ I am deliberately **not** naming a level — derive it from the class and say which class you decided it is. Commit trailers **model-free**: `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` plus a `Claude-Session:` line. English. If there is a diff, draft PR with `Fixes #19383`; if there is none, report and the seat closes the card on your measurement.

⚠️ If any part of this order is imprecise or contradicts what you measure, **say so and stop rather than silently matching it** — six of this seat's orders were wrong this shift and a dev caught every one.

The landing commit's author date is 2026-09-20T19:07:28Z — the **enqueue** instant, which is the other half of the same pattern.

### Content, with a control that existed on the parent

The diff is purely additive (+306 / −0), so there is no removed line to probe. The honest substitute is the same probe run against **both** refs, plus a control that was already there:

| probe | parent `50bfe137c7` | `origin/main` `7ffddfa494` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EnvironmentsAnyFamilyIsPinned` in the pin file | **0** | **1** |
| `environments-any-family.pin.test.ts` in `index.ts` | **0** | **1** |
| ⭐ control — `unwrapResponse<{ environments: any[]` in `index.ts` | **1** | **1** |

The control is what makes the two zeros readings: it hits on the parent, so the probe mechanism demonstrably works against that ref, and the delivery's absence there is an absence the instrument **could have seen**. `.changeset/19383-environments-any-family-membership-pin.md` is present on `origin/main`.

### What actually landed, and the disagreement that produced it

⭐ The dispatch order sketched **an allow-list over a CONTAINS-any detector. The dev refused that sketch and was right to.** Its three grounds were measurements, not preferences: the population is a function of the hop budget (24 / 43 / 57 / 57 at 3 / 4 / 5 / 6), an unbounded walk OOMs at 8 GB twice before any bound is reached, and the false positives are the ledger-protected caller-shaped class **by name** (`organizations.list`, `oauth.applications.list`). A gate like that could only ever have meant "no `any` within N hops".

What landed instead is a **membership pin**: the 14 names ARE the family, read from the tree, with 7 measured non-members beside them. This seat re-derived that population independently on `origin/main` before accepting — 21 callables, 0 annotated, 14 `any`-carrying — and all four unions matched name for name. The 7 clean members are the control: a predicate stuck on `true` swallows `listDrivers` and `uninstall`, one stuck on `false` empties the other side.

⭐ **The order's own hedge is what made this possible**, and it is the reusable lesson: it said *"do not land a guard unless your census shows the design is trivially settled — and if you think it is, say so explicitly and why."* That escape turned a measured disagreement into a deliverable instead of a deviation. ⛔ This seat will not sketch a design in an order again without one.

### Recorded, not requested

The pin file's docblock states the cost of adding a 15th method as *"add its name to the union below"* — singular. The real cost is up to four edit sites. The friction is the deliverable and every site is a line written on purpose, so this is an imprecision in the prose, ⛔ not a defect in the pin. It was recorded in the ACCEPT (`5751928849`) rather than spent on a round trip: the diff is test-only and a fresh CI cycle on a p3 to sharpen one clause is not proportionate.

### Follow-ons the round named and this seat did NOT file

The dev reported three out-of-scope observations and named a successor for each rather than filing. This seat agrees with all three non-filings and repeats them here so they are findable:

1. `packages/client/exported-any-returns.json`'s `$comment` cites a count (21) that no longer matches the tree (39 unannotated / 2 IS-any / 16 CONTAINS-any / 21 clean), and cites no repo or commit — so it is prose, not a reading. Successor: whoever next edits that ledger.
2. `tsup` erases private field types, so 13 callables read CONTAINS-any in `dist` while clean in source. Nothing is wrong today — the landed ratchet asks IS-any and never descends. Load-bearing only for a successor that widens a **dist-reading** `any` gate.
3. An unbounded structural CONTAINS-any walk of this SDK surface does not terminate in practice. Relevant to anyone proposing that instrument for another package.
